subject: Physics
subtopic: Universal gravitation, free fall and orbital motion
axis_note: ladder_position is a curriculum coordinate. It is never a learner estimate; teaching depth is intrinsic, while practice percentages only route support.

must_contain: Two bodies with force ownership explicit: one gravitational force on each receiver along the centre-to-centre line.
At least one supported/upward/falling comparison showing that gravity persists and does not follow the velocity vector.

controlled_variation.vary: support or motion state of one body
controlled_variation.notice: the gravitational interaction remains present and points toward the source
the force pair rotates/relabels with geometry rather than staying page-down

must_contain: The point-mass or external-spherical model scope stated before using the simple inverse-square relation.
Centre-to-centre distance r, not surface gap, identified before scaling or substitution.
Separate mass-factor and inverse-square distance-factor comparisons.

controlled_variation.hold: both masses and valid source model
controlled_variation.notice: force changes with the inverse square of r

controlled_variation.hold: the other mass and centre distance
controlled_variation.notice: force changes linearly with that mass
gravitational-force direction remains toward the source

must_contain: A clear separation between object-specific gravitational force and local g at a spatial point.
The same test mass shown in gravitational force and in F=ma before cancellation.
A fixed-location comparison of different test masses and a fixed-source comparison of different radii.

controlled_variation.notice: force changes with test mass but local g/free-fall acceleration does not

controlled_variation.vary: centre-distance from the same external source
controlled_variation.notice: local g changes with radius rather than remaining universally 9.8

must_contain: The same unchanged object compared at two locations while mass and local g are shown as separate quantities.
Weight identified explicitly as the local gravitational force W = m g, with force and mass units kept distinct.

controlled_variation.hold: the same object and its mass
controlled_variation.notice: weight changes with local g while mass stays unchanged

controlled_variation.vary: the object's mass at one fixed location
controlled_variation.notice: weight changes in direct proportion to mass at fixed g

must_contain: The zero of gravitational potential energy stated explicitly as infinite separation.
A comparison between bound circular motion and the minimum-energy escape case at the same radius.

controlled_variation.hold: source mass, test mass, and chosen potential-energy zero
controlled_variation.notice: kinetic energy changes while the gravitational potential term is unchanged

controlled_variation.vary: from a circular-orbit case to a just-escape case
controlled_variation.hold: the same launch radius and central mass
controlled_variation.notice: the escape case requires a higher kinetic contribution because its limiting total energy is zero

must_contain: An orbital-plane drawing with position and momentum as in-plane polar vectors and angular momentum shown as an axial vector normal to the plane.
The same orbit shown from the opposite face so the axial direction convention must be applied rather than guessed from clockwise/counter-clockwise words alone.

controlled_variation.vary: the satellite's position around the orbit
controlled_variation.hold: central force directed through the same origin
controlled_variation.notice: the torque arm and force stay collinear, so external torque about the centre remains zero

controlled_variation.vary: the viewing side of the orbital plane
controlled_variation.hold: the physical orbit and sense of motion
controlled_variation.notice: the axial-vector arrow appears reversed to the viewer, while the physical angular-momentum direction is unchanged

family.invariant_demand: Identify source, receiver and model scope; separate force, local g and weight; use centre-to-centre geometry and the correct inverse-square or W = m g relation; then verify direction, units/model meaning and a limiting or counterfactual case.
family.difficult_move: Choosing and scoping the gravitational model before calculation—especially force versus field/local g, centre distance versus surface gap, test-mass independence, and mass versus weight—while keeping higher-depth field/orbit work outside the Grade-9 core.
family.independent_check: Change one controlling quantity mentally: reverse velocity without moving the source (force direction should not follow velocity), double r (inverse-square effect), double test mass at one point (force changes but g does not), or change local g for the same object (weight changes but mass does not).

support_ladder.handed_over: The relevant model is named and the controlling radius or energy reference is identified; the learner still executes the relation and the check.
The interacting bodies and centre-to-centre radius are marked; the learner chooses the model and completes the check.
Only the physical situation and requested quantity are given.

transfer.changed_demand: A spherical source is shown with the receiver outside it, but the problem labels altitude above the surface instead of centre distance.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that the simple external Newtonian relation requires centre-to-centre r rather than altitude alone

transfer.changed_demand: A projectile is moving upward near the same source: determine the gravitational-force direction without using its velocity direction.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that gravity direction follows source-receiver geometry and persists during upward motion

transfer.changed_demand: Two different test masses are placed at the same point; compare local g and gravitational force before either is released.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that local g is source/location dependent while force additionally scales with the chosen test mass

transfer.changed_demand: The same object has half the weight at a second location; infer the local-g ratio without changing the object's mass.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: that W = m g permits solving for the g ratio while mass stays fixed

transfer.changed_demand: A satellite experiences an additional tangential thrust: decide whether angular momentum about the planet is still conserved.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: whether the added force produces a non-zero external torque about the chosen centre

transfer.changed_demand: From a launch at the planet surface, determine whether a stated speed gives a bound orbit, escape, or an impossible energy classification.
transfer.information_not_handed_over: the total-energy threshold that separates bound motion from escape
